title: Transformations: Reflection, Rotation, Translation and Enlargement
seo_title: Year 8 Transformations Worksheets: Reflections, Rotations, Translations with Vectors and Enlargements
standard_text: Identify properties of, and describe the results of, translations, rotations and reflections applied to given figures; identify, describe and construct congruent shapes including on coordinate axes; use scale factors and enlargement.
meta_desc: Free Year 8 transformations worksheets: reflect in x = a, y = b and y = x, rotate 90° and 180°, translate by column vectors, enlarge with a scale factor and describe transformations. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Reflection: mirror line. Rotation: angle, direction, centre. Translation: column vector. Enlargement: scale factor, centre.
key_sub: Reflections, rotations and translations keep the shape the same size (congruent).
body_html:
How it works

  • Reflection: give the mirror line. Each point ends up the same distance on the other side.
  • Rotation: give the angle, the direction (clockwise or anticlockwise) and the centre.
  • Translation: give a column vector — top number across (+ right), bottom number up (+ up).
  • Enlargement: give the scale factor and the centre. Every length is multiplied by the scale factor.

Reflections, rotations and translations give a congruent image. Enlargements give a similar image.

Example

Reflect (3, −2) in the y-axis.

Change the sign of the x-coordinate.

Answer: (−3, −2)

Example

Translate (1, 4) by 3
−5.

1 + 3 = 4 and 4 − 5 = −1.

Answer: (4, −1)

Example

Rotate (2, 5) 180° about the origin.

Change both signs.

Answer: (−2, −5)

Common mistakes

  • Reflecting in the wrong axis: the x-axis is horizontal, so reflecting in it changes the y-coordinate.
  • Rotating the wrong way: anticlockwise is the opposite way to clock hands.
  • Swapping the numbers in a column vector: the top number is the horizontal move.
  • Adding the scale factor instead of multiplying for an enlargement.

faq.q: How do I describe a rotation?
faq.a: Give the angle (90°, 180°…), the direction (clockwise or anticlockwise) and the centre of rotation.

faq.q: What does a column vector mean?
faq.a: The top number is the move across (positive means right) and the bottom number is the move up or down (positive means up).

faq.q: What happens to coordinates when you reflect in y = x?
What is the difference between congruent and similar?
faq.a: Congruent shapes are exactly the same size and shape. Similar shapes are the same shape but can be a different size, as after an enlargement.

items.q: A rectangle 4 cm by 7 cm is enlarged by scale factor 0.5. What are the new side lengths?
items.e: Multiply every length by 0.5: 2 cm by 3.5 cm. (A scale factor below 1 makes the shape smaller.)

items.q: A rectangle 9 cm by 6 cm is enlarged by scale factor 0.5. What are the new side lengths?
items.e: Multiply every length by 0.5: 4.5 cm by 3 cm. (A scale factor below 1 makes the shape smaller.)

items.q: A rectangle 9 cm by 2 cm is enlarged by scale factor 4. What are the new side lengths?
items.e: Multiply every length by 4: 36 cm by 8 cm. (A scale factor below 1 makes the shape smaller.)

items.q: A side of length 12 cm becomes 3 cm after an enlargement. What is the scale factor?
items.e: Scale factor = new length ÷ old length = 3 ÷ 12 = 0.25.

items.q: The point (0, −1) is enlarged by scale factor 3 with centre the origin. Where is its image?

items.e: B is the mirror image of A across the y-axis: a reflection in the y-axis.

items.e: B is upside down in the opposite quadrant: a rotation of 180° about the origin.

items.q: Which transformation can change the size of a shape?
items.e: Only an enlargement changes the size (unless the scale factor is 1).

items.q: After a reflection, rotation or translation, the image is…
items.e: These keep every length and angle, so the image is congruent.

items.q: To describe a rotation fully, you must give…
c: the angle, the direction and the centre
items.e: A full description needs the angle, the direction and the centre.

items.q: To describe an enlargement fully, you must give…
c: the scale factor and the centre
items.e: A full description needs the scale factor and the centre of enlargement.

items.q: A shape is enlarged by scale factor 3. What happens to its angles?
items.e: Enlargement changes lengths, not angles: they stay the same.

items.q: A triangle with perimeter 12 cm is enlarged by scale factor 2.5. What is the new perimeter?
items.e: Every length × 2.5: 12 × 2.5 = 30 cm.

items.q: Point P(3, 1) is translated to P′(−1, 4). What is the translation vector?
items.e:
x: 3 → −1 is −4; y: 1 → 4 is +3: −4
3.

items.q: Which point is unchanged by a reflection in the line y = x?
items.e: Points on the mirror line do not move. (4, 4) is on y = x: (4, 4).

items.q: A shape is rotated 90° clockwise and then another 90° clockwise about the same centre. What single rotation is this?
Which is the same as a rotation of 270° anticlockwise?
items.e: 270° one way ends in the same place as 90° the other way.

items.q: A rectangle 4 cm by 6 cm is enlarged to 10 cm by 15 cm. What is the scale factor?
A shape is enlarged by scale factor ½. What happens to its lengths?
items.e: Scale factor ½ makes every length half as long.

items.q: A point (2, −3) is reflected in the line x = 4. Where is its image?
items.e: 2 is 2 left of the line, so the image is 2 right of it: (6, −3).

items.q: The point (5, 2) is rotated 90° anticlockwise about the origin. Where is its image?
Which transformation could map the letter b onto the letter d?
c: A reflection in a vertical line
items.e: b and d are mirror images: a reflection in a vertical line.

items.q: Which transformation could map the letter b onto the letter q?
c: A reflection in a vertical line
items.e: Turning b upside down gives q: a rotation of 180°.
